title: Casatiello
author: Marco Bellini
desc: A dramatic Neapolitan Easter bread ringed with whole eggs baked directly into the dough, generously studded throughout with cured meats and cheese for a rich, savory holiday centerpiece.
longDesc: Casatiello's whole eggs, nestled into the dough and secured with strips of dough forming a cross over each one, are said to symbolize resurrection for the Easter holiday, and the bread's dense richness reflects its role as a meat-and-cheese-forward centerpiece after the fasting of Lent.
ingredients: 100 g (⅓ cup) lard or olive oil, softened
150 g (5.3 oz) pancetta or ham, diced
150 g (1½ cups) mixed cheese (pecorino and provolone), diced
6 whole raw eggs, in their shells, for baking into the dough
equipment: Kitchen twine or extra dough for securing eggs
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the warm water and let sit for 5 minutes.
Combine the flour, salt, and softened lard, then add the yeast mixture, kneading into a smooth, elastic dough.
Let rise, covered, in a warm place for about 1.5–2 hours, until doubled.
Punch down the dough and knead in the diced salami, pancetta, cheese, and a generous amount of black pepper.
Shape the dough into a ring and place in a well-oiled bundt or ring pan.
Let rise again for about 45 minutes.
Nestle the whole, unpeeled raw eggs into the top of the dough at intervals, pressing them in gently.
Cross two thin strips of reserved dough over each egg to secure it in place.
Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 45–50 minutes until deeply golden, tenting with foil if browning too quickly.
Cool before slicing — the eggs cook through fully during baking.
chefTips: The whole eggs bake and cook fully inside their shells as part of the bread — they're meant to be peeled and eaten as part of each slice.
Crossing dough strips over each egg helps keep them securely in place through the final rise and bake.
A generous amount of black pepper is traditional and helps balance the richness of the meats and cheese.
commonMistakes: Not securing the eggs well enough, causing them to shift or fall out during baking.
Skimping on the meat and cheese filling, which is meant to be generous and is central to the bread's character.
Underbaking, leaving the dense, enriched dough undercooked in the center.
servedWith: As part of an Easter breakfast spread
storage: Store wrapped at room temperature for up to 3 days.
reheating: Not applicable; served at room temperature.
healthBenefits: A good source of protein from the eggs, cured meats, and cheese.
culturalNote: Casatiello is a defining feature of the Neapolitan Easter table, its whole baked-in eggs traditionally understood to symbolize resurrection and rebirth for the holiday.
